api.notes: The trigger: an element or plain text. Text becomes a focusable, dashed-underlined inline trigger.
Cancelable intent event before a user-driven change; `tct-after-open-change` once settled.
The `open` attribute is the initial state; it stays dismissible.
The element owns the state (D-006); `open` is the current value. Hover, focus, tap, Escape and outside press change it after the cancelable intent event.

api.reason: A-xstyle: use class/style, ::part(hover-card) and the tokens.
A-xstyle: `class` goes on the host; the painted card is ::part(hover-card).
A-xstyle: `style` goes on the host; the painted card is ::part(hover-card).

hooks.notes: Escape and outside press through the one document layer stack.

keyboard.action: Focusing the trigger with the keyboard opens the card immediately
Moves focus from the trigger into the card's interactive content; the card stays open while focus is inside it
Closes the card; focus returns to the trigger when it was inside the card, and refocusing the trigger does not reopen it

differences.text: `isEnabled` is `disabled`, `hasHoverIndication` (`'auto' | boolean`) is the enumerated `hover-indication` (`auto`, `always`, `never`), `delay`/`hideDelay`/`focusTrigger`/`touchTrigger` keep their names in kebab case (A§7.2).

The controlled `isOpen` / uncontrolled `isDefaultOpen` split collapses into the element-owned `open` state (D-006): the `open` attribute is the default-open state, and setting `open` never emits events.

The card lives in the hover card's shadow root, so a slotted trigger cannot reference it by ID. A labelled card keeps aria-haspopup=dialog and (where the trigger's role allows it) aria-expanded, but drops aria-controls; an unlabelled group card is exposed to a slotted trigger as `aria-description` (a copy of its text) instead of aria-describedby. A text trigger, which shares the shadow root, keeps aria-controls / aria-describedby.

Focus moving from the trigger into the card keeps it open, and focus leaving the card to anything but the trigger closes it, so a keyboard user can operate interactive card content (WCAG 1.4.13 persistent, hoverable, dismissible).
Same Tecton surface as the popover: a 1px border on the recessed popover fill, no drop shadow, 8px container radius (D-013). Upstream paints the surface fill with a medium shadow.
The React portal correction for cards inside a paragraph, heading or link is unnecessary: the card is a top-layer popover in the element's shadow root and never nests in the trigger's parent.

core.hover-card.notes: Guides: [mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips] [mwg:animate-to-from-top-layer] [mwg:position-aware-tooltips]. Has no localisable strings (upstream has none). The layer is kind 'hint' so the controller sets no trigger ARIA and the card owns it.
